title: Lighting an open-plan office
subtitle: BSE3125 Optics and Lighting | Mini lighting design exercise | Semester 1, 2026/27

sections.title: Design basis and spatial interpretation
paragraphs: The proposal provides maintained electric lighting for ordinary office paperwork, typing and data processing: 500 lx average on each task, Uo >= 0.60, directional UGR <= 19 and Ra >= 80 [1,2]. The fixed proposed arrangement comprises 112 desks in 28 four-person benches. Workstations are design assumptions because the supplied drawing does not define furniture. All desks are assessed individually; a room average is insufficient to demonstrate their performance.

Office-facing wall boundaries define the L-shaped office around the northern service core. The measured gross polygon is 1042.10 m2; subtracting eight source-linked column intersections gives 1032.57 m2. The separate 1022 m2 drawing annotation is not a verified boundary area; its smaller value is used conservatively only for lighting power density. Core door gaps are bridged and the core is excluded. Original drawing inputs remain unchanged.

Specified assumptions are a 2.8 m ceiling, 0.8 m desk plane, 1.2 m seated eyes, reflectances of 80/70/20% for ceiling/walls/floor and 40% for columns. Opaque facade walls represent an electric-light condition; actual glazing and daylight are unknown. Desks are calculation planes, not solid furniture. Partitions, monitors and cabinets are not modelled as obstructions. Confirm these assumptions after fit-out.

Each desk is 1.6 x 0.8 m; four desks form a 3.2 x 1.6 m bench. Proposed clearances are at least 0.9 m to walls/columns and 1.8 m between benches. Within bench Bn, Desk-(4n-3), -(4n-2), -(4n-1), -4n occupy SW, SE, NW and NE respectively. These planning clearances do not establish escape-route or accessibility compliance.

sections.title: DIALux functions and calculation method
paragraphs: Import the architectural DXF in metres, check its 45 m overall dimension and trace the office-facing contour. Reconstruct eight full-height columns, set room height/material reflectances, import the manufacturer's ULD photometry, and arrange luminaires on complete 600 mm ceiling tiles. Review the geometry and emitting-plane height in 3D. Native calculation, calculation objects, result tables, isolux diagrams and directional glare plots are used to evaluate the design [3].

DIALux evaluates direct light from the imported intensity distribution together with light reflected by the modelled surfaces. The high wall/ceiling reflectances therefore affect both useful illuminance and the background against which bright luminaires are seen. They are specified finishes, not existing measurements. A fixed maintenance factor of 0.80 converts initial illuminance to the reported maintained illuminance; it does not replace the angular glare calculation.

For each 1.6 x 0.8 m desk, the regular grid has 10 x 5 cells with nominal 0.16 m spacing. EN clause 5.4 gives p = 0.2 d^0.7; the aspect ratio is 2, so d = 0.8 m and p = 0.171 m. The selected spacing is finer. Uniformity is point minimum divided by surface mean, not minimum divided by maximum. All 112 desk means and uniformities are extracted from the native room-scoped tables.

Room glare is calculated at each desk centre at 1.2 m in 15-degree directions, as taught [1]. UGR depends on source luminance, apparent size, position and background luminance; the product's catalogue UGR 16 is not the calculated office glare. The maximum over all tested views is reported. The core project retains directional glare; a separate supplemental project with identical fixtures adds cylindrical, surrounding, background and exposed-surface checks.

All simulation results come from native DIALux calculations; analytical sensitivities and manufacturer declarations are identified separately. Each project is saved, closed and reopened; the reopened tables are compared with the original calculated output. Manufacturer photometry, fixture positions, maintenance factors and physical geometry are checked between projects. Editable native/CAD sources and complete raw outputs are retained separately.

sections.title: Luminaire selection and ceiling coordination
paragraphs: Select 186 Philips PowerBalance gen2 RC461B 40S/840 SEIA W60L60 VPC U4 WH SC UE, order code 910505103638: 4000 lm, 23 W, 4000 K, Ra > 80 and approximately 173.9 lm/W [4]. Manufacturer ULD and LDT files supply the actual photometry. The recessed low-glare optic supports ordinary office tasks; the Interact Ready SC200/DALI-2 D4i product provides a wireless dimming/control route. PstLM 1 and SVM 0.4 are manufacturer declarations, not measured project results.

The 86-degree beam gives an illustrative footprint about 3.73 m wide at the desk plane, 2.0 m below the emitting face. Typical 2.4 m fixture spacing provides overlap, while interreflection supports brightness between fixtures. This geometric illustration is not a lux prediction: the actual intensity distribution and room calculation establish performance. The polar plot shows angular distribution rather than an assumption of uniform downward light.

The 597 x 597 mm body suits the 600 mm ceiling module. Manufacturer data are internally inconsistent on depth: the mechanical table gives 82 mm and the dimension drawing reaches 86 mm. Allow at least the larger 86 mm envelope plus driver, support and service clearance, subject to supplier confirmation. The imported native body is simplified (about 70 mm); its reference z = 2.868 m places the emitting face approximately at the 2.8 m ceiling. Do not interpret that reference as a suspended face.

Every fixture is centred on a complete source ceiling tile. L120 is moved one 600 mm module south to recover the desk affected by grid snapping; positions remain identical in both final native projects and the independent CAD layout. L01 supplies all fixture IDs, desk mapping, ceiling grid, legend and manufacturer schedule.

sections.title: Iteration and spatial performance
paragraphs: The early 142-fixture CoreLine trial had a general working-plane mean around 501 lx but diagnostic desk means of 479/516 lx and UGR 20.3. Changing to the lower-glare PowerBalance optic addressed glare, while increasing the count addressed deficient tasks. Grid snapping then caused Desk-084 to fall to 497 lx; moving L120 recovered it. The nominal 3400 lm design passed, but its 504 lx controlling mean left only 0.8% margin.

The manufacturer declares +/-10% luminous-flux tolerance. A common 10% reduction would lower that 504 lx mean to 453.6 lx. The final 4000 lm variant was therefore imported and freshly calculated at the same 186 positions. It raises the minimum desk mean to 593 lx while keeping maximum directional UGR at 18.1. The mean of the 112 desk means is 659.47 lx; this is not the whole-floor average.

The controlling locations differ: Desk-021 has mean/min/max 593/525/637 lx and Uo 0.89; Desk-084 controls Uo at 0.80 (654/521/736 lx); Desk-018 controls UGR at 18.1 facing 180 degrees. The general adaptive working-plane minimum is not substituted for these fixed task checks. All declared tasks remain included, and the separate usable surrounding/background regions cover the non-task assessment.

sections.title: Controls, power and operation
paragraphs: Provide 32 independent local manual on/off/dim zones: 28 bench zones and four circulation zones. The maximum area is 46.67 m2. Every fixture belongs to exactly one zone. BEC 2024 Table 5.5 requires 32 manual points on the unreduced 1032.57 m2 basis; no reduced count is claimed. Specify compatible sensor/group configuration and confirm coverage at the installed height [5].

During occupied hours, manual ON and daylight dimming must maintain at least 500 lx at the worst served task. Manual OFF takes priority. After 10 minutes without occupancy, command 0% light output; drivers and wireless sensors may retain standby consumption. Commission automatic electrical-power reduction of at least 50%, including standby and accessory loads. A calendar sweep switches off outside working periods; a local after-hours override expires within 120 minutes. Use full-output fallback for sensor faults affecting occupied task lighting.

Where facade review identifies qualifying daylight zones, provide separately controlled daylight sensing/dimming under clause 5.6.2, including the >=5 m2 fenestration trigger and required zone extent. Window dimensions are unavailable, so no daylight illuminance or saving is credited. Verify the trigger, sensor location, zoning and minimum occupied task illuminance after the facade is known.

The conservative power budget is 186 x 23 W + 50 W external-control allowance = 4328 W; LPD = 4328/1022 = 4.235 W/m2, below 7.2 W/m2. Native fixture power is 4278 W and its gross-area denominator differs. The explicit allowance and smaller area explain the higher reported budget. Final accessory loads must stay within the allowance or the budget must be revised. Annual energy saving is not quantified without working hours, occupancy and daylight data.

sections.title: Robustness, maintenance and visual comfort
paragraphs: A common -10% flux sensitivity gives 593 x 0.90 = 533.7 lx at the controlling desk; Uo is unchanged by a common scalar. For +10% source brightness, with background also scaling, the UGR expression gives an approximate change of 8 log10(1.1) = 0.33, or 18.43 from 18.1. These are analytical sensitivities, not separate native simulations or a guarantee for unequal fixture tolerances. At +10% luminaire power, the budget becomes 4755.8 W including 50 W controls, or 4.653 W/m2.

MF = 0.90 lumen maintenance x 1.00 survival x 0.95 luminaire cleanliness x 0.94 surface maintenance = 0.8037, rounded down to 0.80. L90 at 50,000 h is manufacturer-declared; the other factors are design assumptions. Specify annual optical cleaning, prompt failed-unit replacement and three-yearly finish inspection/repainting as needed. Reassess maintenance for actual soiling and hours. L85 at 100,000 h alone does not establish installation MF [4].

For positive-polarity medium-luminance office displays (<=200 cd/m2; tilt <=15 degrees), adopt 1500 cd/m2 under EN clause 5.9.2. Using the manufacturer LDT and 510 x 510 mm emitting aperture, sampled luminance L = I/(A cos gamma) peaks at 1334 cd/m2 (C44, gamma65); +10% flux gives 1468 cd/m2. The check covers supplied samples at gamma65-89 degrees and C0-90 with quadrant symmetry. It cannot establish between-sample maxima or the 90-degree endpoint; full angular conformity remains unverified. Review screen orientation and reflected luminaire images after fit-out.

sections.title: Design conclusion and verification
paragraphs: The proposed 186-luminaire scheme meets the selected task and additional visual-environment criteria in the model: minimum desk mean 593 lx, minimum desk Uo 0.80, maximum tested directional UGR 18.1 and conservative LPD 4.235 W/m2. The higher-output revision trades a moderate power increase for useful illuminance margin while retaining the low-glare optic and coordinated ceiling positions.

Before construction, confirm facade glazing, finish reflectances, plenum depth, actual workstations/obstructions and display characteristics. Commission product identity, tile positions, emitting height, illuminance, seated-view glare, manual controls, occupancy timing, standby-inclusive power reduction, override expiry and daylight response. Recalculate if those inputs change. BEC 2024 is the academic benchmark; statutory applicability depends on the actual building and project timing.

L01 is combined PDF page 9. The appendix guide is page 10; Appendices A and B follow with PDF bookmarks. Original DIALux page numbers printed on native pages are distinct from combined PDF positions. Appendix A contains all 112 task/glare tables and all 186 coordinates; Appendix B contains all 288 supplemental rows and critical surface plots. These are selected original native pages, with full raw output and editable projects retained separately.
